title: The Water That Remembers Both Banks

features.name: the divergent current
features.desc-on-touch: You watch the creek separate into two channels at a stone tongue, each flow remembering its opposite bank. The water hasn't chosen which way it goes — it goes both.

features.name: the stone witness
features.desc-on-touch: A bouldered outcrop between the channels, recording the divergence in its grain. It has watched this split for longer than memory, unmoved.

features.name: the backward echo
features.desc-on-touch: Sound from the left bank arrives at the right shore before the water does, as if the creek is teaching its own geometry how to contradict itself.

features.name: the choice that wasn't made
features.desc-on-touch: A leaf spinning in the confluence, unable to commit to either channel. It will be swept into both currents at once, and the water will remember this indecision.

features.name: the bank that argues with itself
features.desc-on-touch: The earth here has split down its own grain. The western cut remembers eroding. The eastern cut remembers growing. Both are equally right.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the creek where choices unmake themselves
narr: You stand mid-channel with her, the water
current splitting around you both, cold to the
knee. She watches her reflection break into two
paths — one staying, one leaving. "What if," she
says, "nothing has to choose?" The creek answers
by flowing both ways at once.

inscription: the current does not forget which bank it left

file.name: Creekbed_Divergence_Recording_stereoChannels.mp3
file.note: Field recording from a bifurcated creek system in the upper Macleay valley, late afternoon — each channel recorded separately on left and right. The channels drift apart as the recording plays.
